scope: UK employers named in the official report of the UK Parliament (Hansard) in connection with redundancies during the window, whose redundancy programme is confirmed by an ORIGINAL PUBLISHER stating an absolute count of jobs, roles or posts to be cut.

period.date_field: announcement date at the original publisher

assembled_by: Claude Code session, single actor. This manifest has NOT been through the three-actor transcription/matching/publication review chain that docs/RECALL_BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md requires before a recall number may be posted to /benchmarks/recall, and it is therefore NOT published there. NO EVENT HAS BEEN ADJUDICATED.
how_it_was_assembled: 1. FRAME. The official report of the UK Parliament, via the open Hansard search API (hansard-api.parliament.uk), one calendar month per request across 2024-07-01..2026-06-30. TWO fixed terms make up the frame and both were swept COMPLETE over all twelve months: 'redundancies' and 'redundancy'. 218 distinct contributions. The frame was fixed before any tracker query and the tracker was never consulted to choose it.

1b. ENUMERATION CONTROL, PARTIAL AND SAID SO. Two independent phrase queries, "job losses" and "job cuts", were run over the 2025-07..2026-06 half to test whether the frame's vocabulary was missing employers the first two terms did not reach — the same role the '"exit or disposal activities"' control plays in the US set. The Hansard endpoint degraded (25s responses, then read timeouts) and the control reached 2025-11 before it was abandoned. IT IS THEREFORE INCOMPLETE, and the enumeration is NOT claimed to be exhaustive for the window. Whatever the completed portion added is in the frame; what the abandoned portion would have added is UNKNOWN, not zero.

2. WHY THIS FRAME. The UK has no public employer-level equivalent of SEC Form 8-K item 2.05. Its statutory instrument (Form HR1) is published only as monthly aggregates and employer-level release has been refused under FOIA s43; the only complete index of UK regulatory announcements asks agents like this one not to read it; and the two national outlets that could anchor a press frame forbid it in robots/terms. UK-REFERENCE-SET-DEFINITION.md carries the evidence for each.

3. CANDIDATE EXTRACTION. Inside every contribution, sentences carrying a redundancy token were kept, and maximal capitalised spans inside those sentences were taken as employer candidates. Spans made entirely of parliamentary, political or geographic furniture were dropped by a fixed stoplist. 410 candidate spans.

4. CURATION. A single editor kept the spans that name an identifiable EMPLOYER or a named site of one, and dropped places, parties, people, unions and policy names. This step is judgement and is disclosed as such.

5. VERIFICATION AT THE ORIGINAL PUBLISHER. Every surviving candidate was re-checked against the employer's own announcement where one exists, otherwise against a named news organisation's own report. A candidate enters the set only when the original publisher states an ABSOLUTE count in the window. Percentages, retained headcounts, pre-cut totals, derived counts and vague quantities are dropped, which is the same rule extractor.py applies and the same rule the US set used. Every drop is recorded in dropped_candidates with its reason.

6. RE-MEASUREMENT CONTRACT. NOTHING IS ADJUDICATED. Every event is not_matched, so the editor-confirmed numerator is zero by construction. Rows that satisfy the alias/window rule are reported as candidates needing adjudication and are never counted. A machine must not promote its own recall.
why_this_is_independent: The frame is the official report of the UK Parliament. It is not a layoff aggregator, not a commercial data service, not a competitor listing, and it is not a corpus this tracker collects from in any form. No row was selected by searching this tracker and the selection rule was fixed before any tracker query. It is NOT independent of the wider news ecosystem: verification cites news organisations, some of which this tracker also reads. Verification is not enumeration, and the US set has the same property with respect to EDGAR.
known_biases: OVER-REPRESENTS what is politically salient: constituency employers, universities, refineries, steel, shipyards, hospices, councils and the NHS. An MP raises a redundancy programme when it is in the constituency or in the party brief.
UNDER-REPRESENTS London finance, professional services and technology, and foreign multinationals cutting UK white-collar roles, which rarely reach the floor of either House.

The direction of the net bias on recall is NOT known and is not asserted. Politically salient events are more widely reported, which should push measured recall UP; regional and sectoral events are often covered only by local press outside our trusted-domain list, which should push it DOWN.
Parliamentary recess months are thin: August 2025 returned zero contributions for the primary term, so the frame is not uniform across the window.
The curation step in stage 4 is human judgement, not a rule a machine can reproduce byte for byte. The full mechanical candidate list is retained so the step is auditable.

matching_rule.country_basis: any (job location OR employer HQ), the basis the reader's own country filter uses
matching_rule.company_match: token-prefix on the normalised company name after dropping corporate suffixes — imported from recall_goldset, one definition
matching_rule.unreachable_policy: An event whose query could not be completed is UNKNOWN, never a miss.
matching_rule.numerator: events whose match_decision is 'matched'. Nothing is matched yet.
